purpose: Structured JSON for re-import into Excel or other tabular tools

rows.Story: Define and enforce the .NET 10 migration solution boundary
rows.Title: Establish the active migration solution
rows.Implementation Instructions: Use Solutions\WARP_Prototype.Master.sln as the authoritative migration scope. Remove projects that are not part of the target runtime or that cannot be migrated without introducing unnecessary scope.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The solution contains only projects required for the target .NET 10 application and supporting runtime components.
2. Legacy UI, legacy API, obsolete Windows Service host projects, stress-test projects and obsolete test utilities are excluded.
3. The solution loads without missing-project warnings.
4. A clean solution build succeeds.

rows.Story: Define and enforce the .NET 10 migration solution boundary
rows.Title: Remove legacy ExpressUI project from the active solution
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove GUI\ExpressUI\UI.csproj from WARP_Prototype.Master.sln while leaving the source available for historical reference until migration sign-off.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. UI.csproj no longer appears in `dotnet sln ... list`.
2. No active project retains a required project reference to UI.csproj.
3. The solution builds successfully after removal.
4. Any functionality still required from the old UI is represented by a separate backlog item.

rows.Story: Define and enforce the .NET 10 migration solution boundary
rows.Title: Remove legacy WorkflowManager API project from the active solution
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove WorkflowManager\WorkflowManager.API\WorkflowManager.API.csproj from the solution and retain WorkflowManager.API.Core as the target API implementation.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The legacy WorkflowManager.API project is absent from the solution project list.
2. WorkflowManager.API.Core is the only active WorkflowManager API host.
3. No active project references the removed API project.
4. The solution builds successfully.

rows.Story: Define and enforce the .NET 10 migration solution boundary
rows.Title: Remove obsolete worker host projects
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove the legacy *Host projects that are replaced by the .NET 10 daemon projects, including ExpressManagerHost, FileCopierHost, FileDeleterHost, HydraJobManagerHost and RatCatManagerHost.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Obsolete host projects are absent from the solution.
2. Equivalent daemon projects remain present where required.
3. No active project references the removed hosts.
4. Build and deployment documentation no longer relies on the removed projects.

rows.Story: Define and enforce the .NET 10 migration solution boundary
rows.Title: Remove non-production stress and legacy test projects
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove stress-test projects, TestConsole and legacy UnitTests from the active solution. Record replacement testing needs separately rather than carrying incompatible projects into the runtime migration.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The projects are absent from the active solution.
2. Their removal does not remove runtime code required by production projects.
3. The solution builds successfully.
4. Required replacement tests are captured in the validation epic.

rows.Story: Assess the active solution before changing project targets
rows.Title: Inventory active framework, package and configuration dependencies
rows.Implementation Instructions: Run solution-scoped scans against only the projects listed in WARP_Prototype.Master.sln. Identify target frameworks, project formats, framework-only APIs, package references, configuration access, ServiceBuilder usage, Factories references and legacy hosting dependencies.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The inventory is generated from the active solution project list rather than the whole repository.
2. Every active project has entries for target framework, project format, package compatibility, hosting model and configuration model.
3. Framework-specific APIs and unsupported packages are mapped to follow-up backlog tasks.
4. Projects outside WARP_Prototype.Master.sln are excluded unless explicitly brought into scope.

rows.Story: Assess the active solution before changing project targets
rows.Title: Scan active projects for target frameworks and project format
rows.Implementation Instructions: For each active C# project, record whether it is legacy non-SDK or SDK-style, its current target framework declaration, custom imports, assembly-info generation, content/resource handling and any conditional property groups.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Every active C# project is classified as legacy or SDK-style.
2. Current target framework declarations are recorded.
3. Custom imports, generated AssemblyInfo behaviour and resource/content handling are identified.
4. The results identify which projects require SDK-style conversion before multi-targeting.

rows.Story: Assess the active solution before changing project targets
rows.Title: Scan active projects for framework-specific code and legacy dependencies
rows.Implementation Instructions: Search active projects for System.Web, OWIN/Katana, SignalR, Topshelf, ConfigurationManager, App.config/Web.config, Castle Windsor, ServiceBuilder, Factories.csproj, EPPlus, ExcelLibrary and other .NET Framework-specific APIs.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Each hit identifies the active project, source file and usage type.
2. Package references are distinguished from executable code usage.
3. Each confirmed active dependency is assigned a migrate, replace, remove or defer action.
4. No action is created for dependencies found only outside the active solution.

rows.Story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
rows.Title: Enable active projects to build for both .NET Framework 4.8 and .NET 10
rows.Implementation Instructions: Temporarily multi-target eligible active projects to net48 and net10.0 so compatibility issues can be identified and resolved incrementally before removing the .NET Framework target. Preserve the existing net48 runtime behaviour while adding a net10.0 build path.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Each eligible active project declares both net48 and net10.0 in TargetFrameworks.
2. Projects that cannot be multi-targeted are identified and handled through an explicit replacement or host-migration task.
3. Target-specific references and source branches are limited to genuine framework incompatibilities and are clearly documented in the project file or code.
4. The net48 build continues to succeed without behavioural regression.
5. The net10.0 build succeeds for the multi-targeted project set.

rows.Story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
rows.Title: Assess projects for temporary multi-targeting
rows.Implementation Instructions: Review every project retained in WARP_Prototype.Master.sln and classify it as: suitable for net48/net10.0 multi-targeting, requires a replacement .NET 10 host/project, or should be removed from the migration solution. Record framework-specific package, API and hosting constraints.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Every active project has a documented classification.
2. The assessment identifies System.Web, Windows Service hosting, App.config, package compatibility and unsupported API constraints.
3. Projects requiring replacement hosts are linked to separate backlog tasks rather than forced into multi-targeting.
4. The proposed target-framework approach is agreed before project files are changed.

rows.Story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
rows.Title: Convert eligible legacy projects to SDK-style format
rows.Implementation Instructions: Convert eligible non-SDK project files to SDK-style while preserving source inclusion, embedded resources, content files, assembly metadata, project references and build output. Keep business logic unchanged.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Eligible projects use the SDK-style project format.
2. Legacy imports and explicit Compile items are removed only where SDK defaults provide equivalent behaviour.
3. Duplicate AssemblyInfo generation is resolved explicitly.
4. Embedded resources, content files and copy-to-output behaviour remain correct.
5. The existing net48 build still succeeds before net10.0 is added.

rows.Story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
rows.Title: Assess and remediate package compatibility for net10.0
rows.Implementation Instructions: Review every direct package reference in active projects. Upgrade, replace or remove packages that do not support net10.0, while avoiding unnecessary library changes where the existing package remains compatible.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Every active direct package has a documented compatibility outcome.
2. Unsupported packages have a replacement or removal task.
3. Reference-only packages are removed.
4. Licensing implications are reviewed for packages such as Excel libraries where relevant.
5. Restore succeeds for both target frameworks after changes.

rows.Story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
rows.Title: Add net10.0 alongside net48 in eligible projects
rows.Implementation Instructions: Update eligible project files to use `<TargetFrameworks>net48;net10.0</TargetFrameworks>`. Add the minimum conditional package references, framework references and compile conditions required to make both targets build. Do not redesign business logic during this step.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Eligible projects target both net48 and net10.0.
2. Target-specific package and framework references are scoped with explicit conditions.
3. Shared business code remains common between targets wherever possible.
4. Both target builds complete successfully for each converted project.
5. Any remaining incompatibility is captured as a separate migration task with a clear owner and acceptance criteria.

rows.Story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
rows.Title: Preserve SQL projects during the .NET migration
rows.Implementation Instructions: Retain SQL projects in the solution without attempting to assign them a .NET target framework. Verify that database project loading and build behaviour are unaffected by C# project changes.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. SQL projects remain present and load successfully.
2. No .NET TargetFramework property is added to SQL projects.
3. Database scripts, schemas and deployment artefacts remain unchanged unless explicitly required.
4. The complete solution build process handles SQL projects as expected.

rows.Story: Convert active projects to a single supported target framework
rows.Title: Consolidate active projects on net10.0
rows.Implementation Instructions: After the temporary dual-target phase has exposed and resolved compatibility issues, remove net48 from retained projects and eliminate framework-specific compile branches that are no longer required.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Every active C# project targets net10.0 only.
2. No active project contains net48 in TargetFramework or TargetFrameworks.
3. No active source file contains a required `#if NET48` path.
4. A clean restore and solution build succeed.

rows.Story: Convert active projects to a single supported target framework
rows.Title: Replace multi-targeting with net10.0
rows.Implementation Instructions: Update each retained SDK-style project from net48/net10.0 multi-targeting to a single `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>` declaration.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Active project files contain only net10.0 as the target framework.
2. Conditional package or reference groups that only applied to net48 are removed or made unconditional where still needed.
3. Restore completes without target-framework compatibility errors.
4. The complete solution builds.

rows.Story: Convert active projects to a single supported target framework
rows.Title: Remove NET48 conditional code
rows.Implementation Instructions: Review and remove `#if NET48`, `#else` and `#endif` branches that are no longer needed after the solution becomes net10.0-only. Preserve the .NET 10 behaviour path.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. No active code path depends on the NET48 compilation constant.
2. Removed branches do not change the intended .NET 10 behaviour.
3. The solution compiles without preprocessor-related errors.
4. Smoke tests pass for the affected components.

rows.Story: Create the .NET 10 application hosts that replace legacy web and service projects
rows.Title: Establish replacement ASP.NET Core and daemon projects
rows.Implementation Instructions: Create or confirm the .NET 10 replacement projects for ExpressUI.Core, WorkflowManager.API.Core and the daemon hosts. Keep responsibilities equivalent to the legacy hosts and avoid broad architecture redesign.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. ExpressUI.Core and WorkflowManager.API.Core exist as buildable net10.0 projects.
2. Required daemon replacement projects exist and target net10.0.
3. Each replacement project has the project references and configuration required for its current responsibility.
4. Legacy host removal does not leave an unowned runtime responsibility.

rows.Story: Create the .NET 10 application hosts that replace legacy web and service projects
rows.Title: Create or validate ExpressUI.Core host
rows.Implementation Instructions: Configure ExpressUI.Core as the replacement ASP.NET Core application for the required UI-facing API/controller functionality.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The project targets net10.0 and starts through Program.cs.
2. Controllers and routing are enabled.
3. Required shared projects and direct packages are referenced explicitly.
4. The application starts with representative configuration.

rows.Story: Create the .NET 10 application hosts that replace legacy web and service projects
rows.Title: Create or validate WorkflowManager.API.Core host
rows.Implementation Instructions: Configure WorkflowManager.API.Core as the replacement ASP.NET Core API host for selected WorkflowManager endpoints.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The project targets net10.0 and starts through Program.cs.
2. Controllers, routing, JSON options and DI are configured.
3. Required domain and data-access projects are referenced.
4. The API starts and responds to a basic health or test endpoint.

rows.Story: Create the .NET 10 application hosts that replace legacy web and service projects
rows.Title: Create or validate .NET 10 daemon host projects
rows.Implementation Instructions: Ensure ExpressManagerDaemon, HydraJobManagerDaemon, FileCopierDaemon and RatCatManagerDaemon are net10.0 executable projects with equivalent runtime responsibilities to the legacy service hosts.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Each required daemon is present in the active solution.
2. Each daemon targets net10.0 and has an executable Program.cs.
3. Required worker and service references are present.
4. Each daemon can be built independently.

rows.Story: Replace legacy ASP.NET and OWIN startup infrastructure
rows.Title: Move web application startup to ASP.NET Core
rows.Implementation Instructions: Replace Global.asax, System.Web startup and OWIN/Katana bootstrapping with ASP.NET Core Program.cs configuration. Preserve only the hosting, routing, authentication, logging and error-handling behaviour required by active functionality.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Active web hosts use Program.cs and the ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline.
2. Controller routing and JSON behaviour are configured explicitly.
3. Logging and exception handling are available at startup and request time.
4. No active host depends on Global.asax, System.Web or OWIN startup.

rows.Story: Replace legacy ASP.NET and OWIN startup infrastructure
rows.Title: Configure ASP.NET Core routing, JSON, logging and exception handling
rows.Implementation Instructions: Add the minimum middleware and service registrations required for controller discovery, endpoint routing, JSON serialisation, structured logging and consistent exception responses.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Controllers are discovered and mapped.
2. Request/response JSON remains compatible with active clients.
3. Unhandled exceptions are logged and converted to controlled responses.
4. Startup and request logs contain enough context for diagnosis.

rows.Story: Replace legacy ASP.NET and OWIN startup infrastructure
rows.Title: Assess and migrate required authentication and authorisation
rows.Implementation Instructions: Identify which legacy authentication flows are actually required by active endpoints. Implement only the required ASP.NET Core equivalent and do not carry forward unused social providers or unused OWIN packages.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Required authentication mechanisms are explicitly identified.
2. Required endpoints enforce equivalent authorisation rules.
3. Unused cookie, OAuth or third-party provider integrations are not migrated.
4. Authenticated and unauthorised request scenarios are tested.

rows.Story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
rows.Title: Migrate missing ExpressUI functionality to ASP.NET Core
rows.Implementation Instructions: Recreate the required controllers, models, repository contracts and repository implementations in ExpressUI.Core without redesigning the business flow.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Required endpoints exist in ExpressUI.Core with the expected routes and HTTP verbs.
2. Request and response contracts match the legacy behaviour required by the current UI/client.
3. Repository dependencies are resolved through DI.
4. End-to-end business flow completes successfully.

rows.Story: Inventory and prioritise legacy WorkflowManager endpoints
rows.Title: Create an endpoint inventory and select a pilot vertical slice
rows.Implementation Instructions: Inventory legacy WorkflowManager.API endpoints, classify each as migrate, retire or defer, and select a low-risk pilot endpoint to establish the repeatable migration pattern.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Every legacy endpoint is listed with route, verb, controller/action and key dependencies.
2. Each endpoint is classified as migrate, retire or defer.
3. A pilot endpoint is selected with clear rationale.
4. The pilot includes controller, service/domain, data access, configuration and validation concerns.

rows.Story: Inventory and prioritise legacy WorkflowManager endpoints
rows.Title: Build the WorkflowManager endpoint inventory
rows.Implementation Instructions: Extract endpoint information from the legacy API project and capture route, HTTP verb, request model, response model, authentication requirement, domain dependencies and database dependencies.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The inventory covers every controller action in the legacy API project.
2. Duplicate or obsolete endpoints are identified.
3. Dependencies are recorded at sufficient detail to estimate migration effort.
4. The inventory is stored as a project artefact that can be reviewed by the team.

rows.Story: Inventory and prioritise legacy WorkflowManager endpoints
rows.Title: Implement and validate a pilot WorkflowManager endpoint
rows.Implementation Instructions: Migrate one selected endpoint end-to-end into WorkflowManager.API.Core, including route, request/response contracts, DI, domain calls, data access and tests. Use the result as the migration template for remaining endpoints.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The pilot endpoint is callable in WorkflowManager.API.Core.
2. Its request and response behaviour matches the legacy endpoint for representative inputs.
3. Required dependencies are resolved through DI.
4. Database behaviour is equivalent.
5. Lessons from the pilot are reflected in subsequent endpoint tasks.

rows.Story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
rows.Title: Implement LoadImportSelectionData endpoint
rows.Implementation Instructions: Add or correct the controller action responsible for loading import selection data, including the expected route, POST binding and repository call.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The endpoint accepts the expected POST request and no longer returns HTTP 405.
2. Input validation matches the legacy behaviour required by callers.
3. Successful requests return the expected payload shape.
4. Repository failures are handled through the existing error-handling approach.

rows.Story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
rows.Title: Implement DLM selections import repository
rows.Implementation Instructions: Create the concrete repository that implements IDlmSelectionsImportRepository and move the required database calls into the active .NET 10 data-access path.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. A concrete repository implements every interface member.
2. SQL, stored procedure names and parameter mapping preserve legacy behaviour.
3. The repository is registered in DI and can be resolved by the controller.
4. Integration or smoke testing confirms data is returned correctly.

rows.Story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
rows.Title: Implement LoadDlmSubmissionData endpoint
rows.Implementation Instructions: Migrate the controller, request/response models and repository interactions needed to load DLM submission data.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The endpoint is available under the expected route and HTTP verb.
2. Returned data matches the shape required by the consuming UI/client.
3. Invalid or missing input produces a controlled response.
4. The endpoint succeeds against representative data.

rows.Story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
rows.Title: Implement SubmitDlmProfiles endpoint
rows.Implementation Instructions: Migrate the DLM profile submission controller and its supporting repository/service calls into ExpressUI.Core.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Valid submissions are accepted and processed successfully.
2. Validation errors return the expected status and message format.
3. The database operation preserves the existing transaction and error behaviour.
4. A full load-and-submit workflow completes successfully.

rows.Story: Make active projects declare their own direct dependencies
rows.Title: Remove accidental dependency leakage through Factories
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove project references that exist only to make transitive packages available. Add direct package or project references to the projects that actually use those APIs.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Active projects compile without relying on Factories for unrelated transitive dependencies.
2. Direct dependencies are declared in the consuming project.
3. No runtime behaviour changes are introduced.
4. The solution builds and affected workflows pass smoke testing.

rows.Story: Make active projects declare their own direct dependencies
rows.Title: Remove Factories reference from ExpressUI.Core
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove the ExpressUI.Core project reference to Factories after identifying and replacing any transitive dependency that the project was consuming.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. ExpressUI.Core.csproj no longer references Factories.csproj.
2. The project has direct references for every API it uses.
3. All repository classes compile.
4. ExpressUI.Core starts and the migrated endpoints pass smoke testing.

rows.Story: Make active projects declare their own direct dependencies
rows.Title: Add direct Dapper dependency to ExpressUI.Core
rows.Implementation Instructions: Add Dapper directly to ExpressUI.Core because the repository layer uses Query, Execute, DynamicParameters and table-valued parameter extensions.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. ExpressUI.Core declares a direct Dapper package reference.
2. Repository extension methods compile without Factories.
3. The package version is compatible with net10.0.
4. Data-access smoke tests succeed.

rows.Story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
rows.Title: Replace App.config and ConfigurationManager usage
rows.Implementation Instructions: Use appsettings.json, environment variables and Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration for active .NET 10 hosts. Preserve existing setting names and defaults where practical.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Active hosts start without reading App.config or Web.config.
2. Required settings can be supplied through appsettings.json and environment variables.
3. Missing mandatory settings fail with a clear startup error.
4. Environment overrides work without code changes.

rows.Story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
rows.Title: Inventory legacy configuration usage
rows.Implementation Instructions: Scan the active solution for ConfigurationManager.AppSettings, ConnectionStrings, ApplicationSettingsBase, App.config, Web.config and generated Settings classes.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Every active legacy configuration read is listed with project, file and setting name.
2. Each item is classified as migrate, remove or retain temporarily.
3. Inactive files outside the solution are excluded from the migration backlog.
4. Follow-up tasks exist for each active runtime dependency.

rows.Story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
rows.Title: Configure daemon WarpUrl and logging through appsettings.json
rows.Implementation Instructions: Add appsettings.json configuration for Daemon:WarpUrl and AmlinLogging in ExpressManagerDaemon, HydraJobManagerDaemon, FileCopierDaemon and RatCatManagerDaemon.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Each daemon loads configuration through Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.
2. Daemon:WarpUrl and logging settings are available through JSON and environment variables.
3. Startup fails clearly when WarpUrl is required but absent.
4. Each daemon builds and starts using the new configuration path.

rows.Story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
rows.Title: Remove remaining active ConfigurationManager dependencies
rows.Implementation Instructions: Refactor active Factories and WorkflowManager.Domain paths that still obtain settings or connection strings through ConfigurationManager.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. No active source file calls ConfigurationManager for runtime settings.
2. Connection-string and application-setting dependencies are injected or supplied by typed options/factories.
3. Existing setting semantics are preserved.
4. The solution builds and representative runtime paths pass testing.

rows.Story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
rows.Title: Remove or exclude obsolete legacy configuration and generated artefacts
rows.Implementation Instructions: After active configuration reads have been migrated, review App.config files, transforms, generated Settings classes, installer/designer files and legacy AssemblyInfo files. Exclude or delete only after confirming they are not required by build or deployment tooling.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Each legacy artefact is classified as delete, exclude or retain temporarily.
2. Deleted files have no active references.
3. Project files no longer compile obsolete generated code.
4. The solution build and deployment packaging remain successful.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Move active composition to Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection
rows.Implementation Instructions: Replace host-level and worker-level ServiceBuilder calls with constructor injection and small factories for dependencies whose inputs are only known at runtime.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Active hosts compose services through IServiceCollection.
2. Workers do not call static ServiceBuilder methods.
3. Runtime-varying services use explicit factory interfaces.
4. The Factories project can be removed from consumers once no longer required.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Migrate ExpressManagerDaemon host composition to DI
rows.Implementation Instructions: Register the daemon, worker, API service, logging and related services in Program.cs and resolve the daemon from the service provider.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. ExpressManagerDaemon is created by DI rather than direct `new` or ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Constructor dependencies are explicit and null-checked.
3. Program.cs contains all host-level registrations.
4. The daemon starts and completes its existing smoke-test path.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Migrate HydraJobManagerDaemon host composition to DI
rows.Implementation Instructions: Replace direct ServiceBuilder construction in the Hydra job daemon host with IServiceCollection registrations and constructor injection.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The daemon is resolved from DI.
2. Host-level ServiceBuilder calls are removed.
3. Existing worker and API service lifetimes are preserved.
4. The daemon starts and the existing smoke-test scenario succeeds.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Migrate FileCopierDaemon host composition to DI
rows.Implementation Instructions: Register FileCopyWorker, WorkerService, WorkflowManagerApiService, logging and the daemon itself through Microsoft DI.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. FileCopierDaemon receives IWorkerService and logger through constructor injection.
2. FileCopierDaemon.csproj has no unnecessary Factories reference.
3. The solution builds.
4. A file-copy smoke test is completed when a representative workflow is available, or the limitation is documented.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Remove stale Factories project reference from FileCopierDaemon
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove the FileCopierDaemon project reference to Factories after host-level ServiceBuilder usage has been eliminated and direct dependencies are declared.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. FileCopierDaemon.csproj no longer references Factories.csproj.
2. FileCopierDaemon source does not import MSAmlin.Express.Factories.
3. The daemon project and full solution build successfully.
4. DI registrations still resolve at startup.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Migrate RatCatManagerDaemon host composition to DI
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove host-level ServiceBuilder use from RatCatManagerDaemon and resolve the daemon and its host dependencies through Microsoft DI.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The daemon host has no direct ServiceBuilder construction.
2. The solution builds successfully.
3. Runtime behaviour is preserved where it can be verified.
4. The lack of an active RatCat workflow is recorded as a release risk if testing cannot be completed.

rows.Story: Preserve operational behaviour while modernising daemon hosts
rows.Title: Preserve daemon startup, shutdown and worker-thread behaviour
rows.Implementation Instructions: Ensure the .NET 10 daemons retain the operational semantics of the legacy service hosts, including startup logging, worker-thread creation, shutdown signalling, graceful join and exception handling.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Each daemon starts its worker path exactly once.
2. Shutdown signals are observed and worker threads terminate within the agreed timeout.
3. Startup, shutdown and unhandled exceptions are logged.
4. No daemon leaves foreground threads or undisposed services after shutdown.

rows.Story: Preserve operational behaviour while modernising daemon hosts
rows.Title: Validate daemon lifecycle and service-hosting assumptions
rows.Implementation Instructions: Review Program.cs and daemon classes for startup, cancellation, thread lifetime, disposal and deployment expectations. Confirm whether each daemon will run as a console process, scheduled process or managed Windows service.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Hosting mode is documented for each daemon.
2. Start and stop paths are testable without forcefully terminating the process.
3. Thread joins and timeouts are explicit.
4. Disposable services and service providers are disposed correctly.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Create task-message creator factory
rows.Implementation Instructions: Add ITaskMessageCreatorFactory in ServiceInterfaces and TaskMessageCreatorFactory in Services. Use the factory where task ID, task type and worker type are only known at execution time.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The interface exposes a Create method with task ID, task type and worker type.
2. The implementation returns the same concrete task-message creator previously produced by ServiceBuilder.
3. The factory is registered in each required host.
4. Worker code no longer calls ServiceBuilder for task-message creation.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Create file-copy service factory
rows.Implementation Instructions: Add IFileCopyServiceFactory in ServiceInterfaces and FileCopyServiceFactory in Services. Use it to create disposable file-copy service instances per operation.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The factory returns an IFileCopyService configured with the existing progress-reporting copier.
2. FileCopyWorker receives the factory through its constructor.
3. Each copy operation creates and disposes its own service instance.
4. FileCopyWorker contains no ServiceBuilder call.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Refactor Worker<T> and DatabaseWorker<T>
rows.Implementation Instructions: Inject task-message and database-service factories into the abstract worker hierarchy. Preserve task-specific server selection and message creation.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Worker<T> no longer imports MSAmlin.Express.Factories.
2. DatabaseWorker<T> obtains database services through an injected factory using task.ServerName.
3. Derived worker constructors are updated consistently.
4. Existing worker behaviour and error messages remain unchanged.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Refactor ExpressTaskRunner
rows.Implementation Instructions: Replace ServiceBuilder calls for express service, task-message creator and database service with injected factory abstractions.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. ExpressTaskRunner contains no ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Server-specific services are created using the task's server name.
3. Existing disposal and lifetime behaviour are preserved.
4. ExpressManagerDaemon smoke tests pass.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Refactor HydraJobWorker
rows.Implementation Instructions: Replace ServiceBuilder calls for WorkflowManager API services, Hydra job database services and general database services with injected services and factories.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. HydraJobWorker contains no ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Per-server Hydra job database services are created through a factory.
3. WorkflowManager API dependencies are injected with the correct worker identity and URL.
4. HydraJobManagerDaemon smoke tests pass.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Refactor RatCatWorker
rows.Implementation Instructions: Replace ServiceBuilder calls for RatCat database service, name validation and database attacher creation with explicit injected abstractions.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. RatCatWorker contains no ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Runtime-specific database attacher creation uses an explicit factory.
3. Existing validation and database attachment logic is unchanged.
4. The solution builds and the limited testability is recorded.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Remove Factories reference from Workers
rows.Implementation Instructions: Remove Workers.csproj's reference to Factories.csproj after all active ServiceBuilder and Factories namespace usage has been eliminated.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Workers.csproj no longer references Factories.csproj.
2. No source file in Workers imports MSAmlin.Express.Factories.
3. The project builds independently.
4. The complete solution and migrated daemon smoke tests pass.

rows.Story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
rows.Title: Refactor WorkflowManager.Domain ServiceBuilder usage
rows.Implementation Instructions: Treat WorkflowManager.Domain.ServiceBuilder as a separate cleanup stream. Replace active calls in ErrorService and task-success handlers with constructor injection or narrow factories.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Active domain services and handlers contain no static ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Sproto DAL and task-creator dependencies are explicit.
3. Commented-out legacy calls are removed or retained only with a justified note.
4. WorkflowManager.API.Core integration tests pass.

rows.Story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
rows.Title: Classify legacy package usage within WARP_Prototype.Master.sln
rows.Implementation Instructions: Scan only projects currently included in WARP_Prototype.Master.sln and classify each legacy package as active runtime usage, reference-only, or absent.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. The scan is generated from `dotnet sln ... list` rather than the whole repository.
2. Katana/OWIN, SignalR 2.2, Topshelf, EPPlus, ExcelLibrary, Castle Windsor and ServiceBuilder are covered.
3. Each result names the active project and file.
4. No conclusion relies on projects outside the active solution.

rows.Story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
rows.Title: Verify Katana and SignalR are absent from active projects
rows.Implementation Instructions: Search active solution projects for Microsoft.Owin, Owin, IAppBuilder, OwinStartup, SignalR packages, Hub types and SignalR client APIs.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Results are limited to active solution projects.
2. Any active code usage is listed separately from package-only references.
3. If no hits exist, the backlog records these as non-blocking for the active migration.
4. Build files are checked as well as source code.

rows.Story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
rows.Title: Verify Topshelf usage
rows.Implementation Instructions: Search active solution projects for Topshelf package references, HostFactory calls and Topshelf namespace imports.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. No active usage is assumed without a concrete file-level hit.
2. Any hit identifies whether it is package-only or executable code.
3. If no hits are found, no Topshelf replacement task is created.
4. The conclusion is documented in the migration scope.

rows.Story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
rows.Title: Verify EPPlus and ExcelLibrary usage
rows.Implementation Instructions: Search active solution projects for package references and concrete APIs such as OfficeOpenXml, ExcelPackage and ExcelLibrary workbook types.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Active code usage is distinguished from stale references.
2. Any required Excel export/import path is assigned a compatibility or replacement task.
3. Reference-only packages are removed from active project files.
4. Projects outside WARP_Prototype.Master.sln are ignored.

rows.Story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
rows.Title: Quantify Castle Windsor and ServiceBuilder coverage
rows.Implementation Instructions: Count active files and call sites that use Castle Windsor and ServiceBuilder. Report host-level, worker-level and domain-level coverage separately.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Castle Windsor results include package references, container creation, installers and registrations.
2. ServiceBuilder results include every active static call and Factories project reference.
3. Coverage is grouped by active project and runtime layer.
4. The DI migration backlog is updated only from confirmed active usage.

rows.Story: Prove that the migration retains existing business and integration behaviour
rows.Title: Define behaviour-preservation checks for migrated components
rows.Implementation Instructions: Create explicit compatibility checks for HTTP routes and verbs, DTO shapes, SQL/stored procedure calls, task messages, worker identity, progress events, configuration defaults, service lifetimes and disposal.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Each migrated component has a defined legacy-vs-.NET-10 comparison.
2. HTTP routes, verbs and payload shapes remain compatible where required.
3. Database calls and parameter mappings remain unchanged unless an approved change exists.
4. Worker messages, progress events and service lifetimes remain equivalent.

rows.Story: Prove that the migration retains existing business and integration behaviour
rows.Title: Create component-level compatibility checklists
rows.Implementation Instructions: For each migrated web endpoint, daemon and worker, document the observable legacy behaviour and the corresponding .NET 10 behaviour to be verified during testing.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Checklists exist for migrated endpoints, daemons and workers.
2. Each checklist includes inputs, outputs, side effects, logging and failure behaviour.
3. Any intentional difference is approved and linked to a decision.
4. The checklists are referenced by smoke, SIT and regression test tasks.

rows.Story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
rows.Title: Complete technical and business validation
rows.Implementation Instructions: Verify compilation, startup, business workflows and non-functional requirements. Treat the migrated branch as a reference implementation until the required release testing is complete.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Clean restore and build succeed in the target build environment.
2. Required web/API and daemon smoke tests pass.
3. SIT and regression tests cover the agreed business scope.
4. Performance, security and operational checks are complete before production approval.

rows.Story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
rows.Title: Run clean restore and full solution build
rows.Implementation Instructions: Delete or isolate generated output as appropriate, restore dependencies and build WARP_Prototype.Master.sln using the target .NET 10 SDK.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. `dotnet restore` completes successfully.
2. `dotnet build` completes with zero errors.
3. New warnings are reviewed and either resolved or accepted with justification.
4. The build uses only supported active projects.

rows.Story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
rows.Title: Run ExpressUI.Core and WorkflowManager.API.Core smoke tests
rows.Implementation Instructions: Start both applications with representative configuration and exercise the migrated endpoints and primary DLM workflow.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Both applications start without unhandled exceptions.
2. Health/startup checks complete successfully.
3. Load import selection, load submission data and submit profiles endpoints return expected results.
4. Logs contain no new migration-related errors.

rows.Story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
rows.Title: Run daemon smoke tests
rows.Implementation Instructions: Start and exercise ExpressManagerDaemon and HydraJobManagerDaemon. Test FileCopierDaemon and RatCatManagerDaemon when representative workflows and environments are available.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. ExpressManagerDaemon starts and processes a representative task.
2. HydraJobManagerDaemon starts and processes a representative task.
3. FileCopierDaemon and RatCatManagerDaemon are either tested successfully or recorded as explicit release risks.
4. Shutdown behaviour is clean and no worker threads are abandoned.

rows.Story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
rows.Title: Complete SIT and regression testing
rows.Implementation Instructions: Execute the agreed business regression pack across UI, API, database and daemon workflows using representative environments and data.
rows.Acceptance Criteria:
1. Test scope and entry/exit criteria are agreed.
2. All critical and high-priority scenarios pass.
3. Defects are triaged and blocking defects are resolved.
4. Business and technical owners approve the test outcome.
